title: Grateful Dead Live at Avalon Ballroom on 1969-01-26
lineage: Dat (Sony R500) -> Sound Devices 744T -> Samplitude Professional v11.03 -> FLAC

ai_review.summary: A crisp soundboard transfer captures a quintessential early‑'69 Avalon show, highlighted by a soaring Clementine, Death Don't Have No Mercy and The Eleven.
ai_review.review: The Miller‑sourced SBD has been freshly transferred and, despite a few early‑mix hiccups, offers one of the clearest 1969 recordings on the Archive. Musically the night is a high‑energy snapshot of the band’s heavy‑psychedelic peak – Clementine, Death Don’t Have No Mercy, The Eleven and Turn On Your Love Light are repeatedly praised, while Dark Star and St. Stephen are seen as merely adequate.

ai_rating.rationale: The majority of reviews (13/15) give 4‑5 stars, lauding both the performance and the improved transfer; a few note mix issues but they do not outweigh the overall enthusiasm.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Fresh Miller transfer is praised as crisp and one of the best on the Archive. Reviewers mention early‑mix problems and occasional dip in clarity, but overall the sound is clear, balanced and the keyboards sit prominently in the mix.

show_quality.setlist_flow: First set is tight and focused; the second set builds into a psychedelic peak with seamless transitions, especially from The Eleven into Lovelight.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Praised for bluesy lead on Death Don't, confident vocals and powerful soloing throughout.
band_member_comments.Phil: Noted for leading the riff section in Clementine and delivering strong bass lines (“Phil bombs”).
band_member_comments.Keys: Tom Constanten’s organ/arpeggios receive special mention for adding trippy layers and being front‑and‑center in the mix.
band_member_comments.Drums: Both drummers are described as pounding and driving the intensity of the performance.
